subject: Control plane identity & service-account handoff: SSO + SCIM next steps
messages:
From: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@fincorp.com>
To: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fincorp.com, okta-admin@fincorp.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Control plane identity handoff — initial artifacts and timeline

Hi Dev / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As discussed, we want to hand off the identity integration work for our Private Control Plane deployment. High level asks from our side:

- SAML SSO (IdP initiated + SP initiated) for console access to the private control plane endpoints
- SCIM provisioning for user + group sync (Okta -> Redwood control plane)
- Mapping of Okta groups to Redwood IAM roles (least-privilege templates for dev/ops/sec)
- Service account model for machine-to-machine calls (CI/CD, data pipelines) and rotation cadence

Attached: "mutual-action-plan.pdf" (high-level timeline) and a sample of our IdP metadata.

Can you confirm the exact artifacts you need (cert format, single logout support, SCIM attribute mapping) and whether Redwood will support scoped SCIM tokens for delegated provisioning? We have an internal security review window starting 4/26 and would like the bulk of the integration done by then.

Thanks,
Alice Murphy
Director, Cloud Ops — FinCorp
security@fincorp.com

---
From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@fincorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane identity handoff — initial artifacts and timeline

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and the MAP. We're aligned on scope. Quick checklist of what we'll need from FinCorp to start the Private Control Plane identity work:

1) IdP SAML metadata (XML) with certificate(s) and an endpoint we can test against (IdP test instance preferred)
2) SCIM service account details: the token type you want to delegate (bearer token) and whether FinCorp prefers incremental sync vs full sync on first run
3) Okta group names and desired mapping to Redwood roles (example CSV is fine)
4) Proxy/egress constraints: our control plane needs to initiate outbound to your IdP/SCIM endpoints from a private subnet — please confirm IP allowlist or proxy host + auth
5) Certificate rotation window and preferred notification cadence (we recommend 30-day rotation for SCIM tokens, cert rotation per your policy)

Internally we'll do:
- Create ephemeral service-account model for admin/API clients with scoped KMS-wrapped keys for the private control plane
- Implement SCIM with support for group-member provisioning + delta syncs; we support deprovision events mapped to access revocation
- Add a SAML assertion validator that reads NameID vs. attribute-based identifiers depending on your preference (we can map either)

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical handoff call this Thursday 4/15 at 10am PT — I'll send a calendar invite. I'll bring Rishi (engineering lead) and Marissa (solutions) to cover perf and deployment runbooks.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@fincorp.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane identity handoff — initial artifacts and timeline

Hi Alice — good to meet this morning (quick notes below). My note on the architecture:

- Control plane will accept SAML assertions at the private SP endpoint (HTTPS inside your VPC peering/privatelink). We'll publish SP metadata; you can upload this into Okta.
- SCIM connector runs as an outbound-only egress from the control plane to your Okta SCIM API. If you require inbound connectivity, we can set up a tunneled reverse-proxy — but outbound is strongly preferred.
- For machine/service accounts, we recommend a short-lived token model: Redwood issues a signed JWT for service accounts that is validated by the control plane. Keys are stored and rotated in your KMS (we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS).
- Group->Role mapping: our recommended baseline is: "fincorp-admins" => Admin role (no billing permissions), "fincorp-ops" => Operator role, "fincorp-viewers" => ReadOnly. We can provide a mapping template (CSV).

Attached: "private-sso-arch-diagram.png" (deployment sketch). Security notes: we will emit audit events for SAML logins and SCIM provisioning actions to your audit collector (syslog/CloudWatch endpoint) — please confirm the format you prefer.

Open question from our security team: will FinCorp require SAML assertions with EncryptedAttributes, or do you want signed-only? Also confirm whether NameID will be email or persistent ID for your org.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

---
From: Alice Murphy <alice.murphy@fincorp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fincorp.com, okta-admin@fincorp.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane identity handoff — initial artifacts and timeline

Laura / Dev — thanks for the diagram and call notes. Quick answers:

- We'll provide SAML metadata (XML) and an Okta test tenant by 4/22.
- EncryptedAttributes: not required for phase 1 — signed assertions are fine. NameID will be email for directory users; persistent ID for service accounts if needed.
- We prefer outbound SCIM from Redwood to Okta API; our proxy team will provide proxy host + auth header for egress.

One operational constraint: our security team requires that all SCIM operations go through a dedicated service account and that account's token is rotated every 45 days. Can Redwood support scoped SCIM tokens and a rotation webhook so we can confirm key rotation events?

Also, can Redwood's SAML SP support HTTP-Redirect binding for SSO and POST for Assertion Consumer Service? We need both for compatibility with our portals.

Alice

Hi all — putting the technical action items and owner matrix in one place so the security review window (week of 4/26) is covered. I'll drive engineering tasks.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- FinCorp: deliver IdP SAML metadata XML + test tenant (okta-admin / 2027-04-22) [Alice]
- FinCorp: provide proxy egress details and allowlist IPs or proxy credentials (2027-04-23) [security@fincorp.com]
- Redwood (Eng): generate SP metadata and share ACS / SLO endpoints and cert (2027-04-24) [Rishi]
- Redwood (Eng): SCIM connector initial deploy (outbound) with scoped token support + rotation webhook (2027-04-26) [Rishi / Dev]
- Redwood (PM): finalize group->role mapping CSV and mutual action plan (2027-04-23) [Laura / Marissa]
- Both: confirm audit event schema for SAML login and SCIM events (syslog/CloudWatch) (2027-04-25) [All]

Notes / engineering constraints:
- We will implement delta SCIM sync (incremental) for first pass to reduce blast radius; full resync tooling is available on demand.
- Service accounts: Redwood issues short-lived JWTs signed by customer KMS; token exchange will require a service-account binding call that is logged to the audit stream.
- SAML bindings: we support HTTP-Redirect and HTTP-POST for ACS; SP-initiated SSO is supported via RelayState semantics.
- Rotation: we will emit a webhook when we rotate SCIM provisioning tokens; you may optionally call our token-rotate endpoint to request early rotation.

Attachments: scim-provisioning-checklist.xlsx (fields: attribute mapping, delta frequency, admin emails), mutual-action-plan.pdf (timeline + milestones).

I'll follow up with the SP metadata bundle and a small test harness for your Okta test tenant by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference
